questions.title: A dural-based mass shows whorled spindle-cell histology. Which tumour is this?
questions.question: A dural-based intracranial mass, firmly attached to the dura, shows whorled patterns of spindle cells on histology. Which tumour is this?

explanations.A: Correct. Meningioma is a tumour of arachnoid cap cells that arises attached to the dura mater, classically showing whorled (concentric) patterns of spindle-shaped cells on histology. This combination of firm dural attachment and whorled architecture is its classic gross/microscopic recognition pattern. A subset of meningiomas additionally show calcification of whorl centres into psammoma bodies, a separate secondary feature.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Glioblastoma is an intra-axial (within brain parenchyma) tumour showing necrosis and microvascular proliferation, not a dural-based mass with whorled spindle-cell architecture.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Medulloblastoma is a posterior fossa tumour of small, primitive round (embryonal) cells in children, not a dural-based whorled spindle-cell tumour.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Schwannoma arises from Schwann cells of a peripheral or cranial nerve (e.g. vestibular schwannoma), showing Antoni A/B patterns, not the dural whorled pattern of meningioma.

questions.learning_objective: Identify meningioma from its classic dural-based attachment and whorled spindle-cell histological pattern.

questions.title: What behavioural response follows electrical stimulation of the amygdala?
questions.question: In experimental animals, electrical stimulation of the amygdala characteristically produces which behavioural response?

explanations.A: Correct. The amygdala is central to processing and generating fear. Its electrical stimulation in experimental animals produces a stereotyped fear/defensive-avoidance response — freezing, autonomic arousal, avoidance behaviour. Bilateral amygdala lesions instead produce the opposite effect, placidity and blunted fear, as in Klüver-Bucy syndrome.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Hyperphagia is classically associated with lesions of the ventromedial hypothalamus (satiety centre), not amygdala stimulation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Somnolence is not the characteristic response to amygdala stimulation; the reticular activating system, not the amygdala, is central to arousal/sleep regulation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Analgesia is characteristic of periaqueductal grey stimulation (descending pain-inhibitory pathway), not amygdala stimulation, whose hallmark effect is fear/defensive behaviour.

questions.learning_objective: State that stimulation of the amygdala produces a fear/defensive-avoidance behavioural response.

questions.title: What is the recommended empiric antibiotic regimen for suspected bacterial meningitis in an older adult?
questions.question: A 67-year-old presents with fever, neck stiffness and altered consciousness; bacterial meningitis is suspected. Which empiric antibiotic combination is most appropriate while awaiting CSF culture results?

explanations.A: Correct. Empiric therapy combines vancomycin (covering resistant/penicillin-non-susceptible pneumococcus, including MRSA), ceftriaxone (covering typical meningitis pathogens including N. meningitidis and susceptible pneumococcus), and ampicillin, added specifically for Listeria monocytogenes coverage, a concern in patients over about 50 years old, since Listeria is intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Amoxicillin alone would cover Listeria but leaves resistant pneumococcus and most gram-negative meningitis pathogens inadequately treated; it is not sufficient empiric monotherapy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Metronidazole plus gentamicin targets anaerobes and some gram-negatives but does not reliably cover the typical bacterial meningitis pathogens (pneumococcus, meningococcus, Listeria) and is not standard empiric meningitis therapy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Doxycycline plus azithromycin targets atypical organisms and is not standard empiric coverage for acute bacterial meningitis.

questions.learning_objective: State that empiric bacterial meningitis therapy in an older adult combines vancomycin, ceftriaxone and ampicillin, with ampicillin added for Listeria coverage.
